Final categorization: OK  
(Justification: The paper is a non-review research article that explicitly models future Agriculture, Forestry and Other Land Use (AFOLU)—a land use land cover classification—at the national scale for all eight SAARC member countries (Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Nepal, Maldives, Pakistan, Sri Lanka), collectively treated as individual nations within a regional study. The primary objective is to project AFOLU changes to 2050 under four IPCC climate scenarios (RCP 2.6, 4.5, 6.0, 8.5), satisfying the requirement of ≥2 future scenarios with quantitative comparison. The methodology uses multilayer perceptron neural network (MLP-NN) modeling driven by bioclimatic and topographic variables, producing spatially explicit mapped outputs for each country. Model performance is evaluated using quantitative accuracy metrics (AUC of 0.56 for 2007 and 0.87 for 2016 via Total Operating Characteristic analysis). The study meets all core inclusion criteria: national-scale implementation per country, primary focus on LULC prediction, multi-scenario quantitative comparison, spatial modeling with accuracy assessment, and mapped projections. It does not trigger any exclusion criteria—it is not global without disaggregation (it analyzes each nation separately), not local/regional only, includes explicit LULC prediction, and is not methodological without application.)
